title: Relative normalization identifies the quasi-finite locus with an open
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and point sets have the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A morphism is representable when all its pullbacks by schemes are schemes. Separated means that its relative diagonal is representable by closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Integral means representable by integral scheme morphisms [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Quasi-compact means that every pullback by an affine scheme has quasi-compact underlying space. Let $f:V	o Y$ be representable, separated and of finite type: on scheme tests it is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and it is quasi-compact. A factorization $f=
u\circ g$ with $
u:N	o Y$ integral is called the relative normalization factorization here if, for every factorization $f=\pi\circ h$ through an integral morphism $\pi:Z	o Y$, there is exactly one $Y$-morphism $c:N	o Z$ with $c\circ g=h$. Fix a relative normalization factorization $V\xrightarrow{g}N\xrightarrow{
u}Y$ of $f$. Say that $f$ is quasi-finite at $v\in|V|$ if, after an etale scheme chart $T	o Y$ and a lift of $v$ to the scheme $V	imes_YT$, the projection $V	imes_YT	o T$ is quasi-finite at that lift in the sense of [pqf-def-quasifinite]; equivalently this holds at every such lift. There is an open subspace $W\subseteq N$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace] such that $g^{-1}(W)$ is exactly the locus where $f$ is quasi-finite, and the induced morphism $g^{-1}(W)	o W$ is an isomorphism. The inverse image is the open sheaf fibre product $V	imes_NW$ with its induced open-subspace structure.

source.place: Tag 0ABR (lemma-finite-type-separated), with the normalization identified by Tag 0823 (lemma-characterize-normalization).

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $p:T\to Y$. Put $V_T=V\times_YT$ and $N_T=N\times_YT$. These are schemes, since $f$ and $\nu$ are representable; the projections $V_T\to V$ and $N_T\to N$ are surjective etale. The scheme map $f_T:V_T\to T$ is separated and of finite type by the scheme-test hypotheses on $f$: its diagonal is the corresponding test of the closed relative diagonal. The cited etale-base-change theorem gives the integral-factorization universal property for $V_T\to N_T\to T$. Let $V_T\to C_T\to T$ be the concrete scheme normalization. Its integral projection and its universal property give comparison maps $a:N_T\to C_T$ and $b:C_T\to N_T$ commuting with both structure arrows. Uniqueness in each universal property gives $ba=1_{N_T}$ and $ab=1_{C_T}$. Thus this is an isomorphism of factorizations, not merely an isomorphism of the middle schemes.

source.place: Tag 0ABR, first paragraph; Tag 0ABP, and comparison via the characterization Tag 0823

proof.text: Apply the scheme-normalization leaf to $f_T$ and transfer its open along $N_T\simeq C_T$, obtaining $O_T\subseteq N_T$. Write $Q_T$ for the scheme quasi-finite locus of $f_T$. A point of $Q_T$ is isolated in its scheme fibre by the cited quasi-finite-at-point theorem. Conversely, if the fibre point is isolated, choose affine neighbourhoods of it and its image with the source neighbourhood mapping into the target neighbourhood; the cited isolated-fibre affine-pair theorem gives the finite-type quasi-finite ring map required by the definition. Hence the isolated-fibre predicate in the leaf is exactly $Q_T$. We obtain $g_T^{-1}(O_T)=Q_T$ and an isomorphism $g_T^{-1}(O_T)\to O_T$.

source.place: Tag 0ABR, application of Tag 03GW; the point predicate is compared using morphisms.tex Tag 01TH

proof.text: Let $Q\subseteq|V|$ be the quasi-finite locus in the statement. Independence of the target chart follows from common refinement: for charts $T,T^{\prime}\to Y$, the scheme $R=T\times_YT^{\prime}$ exists by the representable diagonal of $Y$. Lifts of the same $v$ have a common lift to $V\times_YR$ by the point fibre-product calculus. Apply the scheme quasi-finiteness base-change equivalence to both projections $R\to T,T^{\prime}$; quasi-finiteness at either lift is therefore equivalent to quasi-finiteness at the common lift. Thus the inverse image of $Q$ under $V_T\to V$ is exactly $Q_T$. It is open by step 2. Since the atlas point map is open and surjective, $Q$ is the image of this open inverse image, hence open. The invariant-open-quotient theorem gives an open subspace $U\subseteq V$ with point set $Q$. Its pullback $U_T$ and $g_T^{-1}(O_T)$ have equal point sets and hence are equal open subspaces. Consequently $U\times_NN_T=U\times_YT=U_T\simeq O_T$, over $N_T$.

source.place: Tag 0ABR, the open quasi-finite part and its base change, expanded using the atlas definition

proof.text: The base change of $g|_U:U\to N$ along the surjective etale scheme atlas $N_T\to N$ is the isomorphism $U_T\to O_T$ followed by the open inclusion $O_T\hookrightarrow N_T$. The etale-local open-immersion theorem therefore says that $g|_U$ is an open immersion. Let $W\subseteq N$ be its image subfunctor: on any scheme test its pullback is the open subscheme identified by that open immersion. Thus $W$ is an open subspace and $U\to W$ is an isomorphism. Pulling back this identification along $N_T\to N$ gives $W\times_NN_T=O_T$, since the local map just described has image $O_T$.

source.place: Tag 0ABR, descent of the open immersion and definition of the image open

proof.text: It remains to check the full inverse image, including points outside $U$. Pulling back $g^{-1}(W)\subseteq V$ along $V_T\to V$ gives $g_T^{-1}(O_T)=U_T$, so its point set and $Q$ have equal inverse images under a surjective point map. Their point sets are equal. Both are open subspaces, hence the point-open calculus gives $g^{-1}(W)=U$ as open subfunctors, with their induced structures. The isomorphism $U\to W$ from the preceding step is therefore exactly the required map $V\times_NW\to W$.

source.place: Tag 0ABR, final omitted verification, written out by the atlas pullback

lean.statement: theorem exists_openSubspace_normalization_quasiFinite_locus {S : Scheme.{u}} {V Y N : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : V ⟶ Y) (hf : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ LocallyOfFiniteType p.left) f.hom.hom) (hsep : MapIsSeparated f) (hqc : MapIsQuasiCompact f.hom.hom) (g : V ⟶ N) (ν : N ⟶ Y) (hfactor : g ≫ ν = f) (hν : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsIntegralHom p.left) ν.hom.hom) (huniv : ∀ (Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (h : V ⟶ Z) (π : Z ⟶ Y), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsIntegralHom p.left) π.hom.hom → h ≫ π = f → ∃! c : N ⟶ Z, g ≫ c = h ∧ c ≫ π = ν) : ∃ W : OpenSubspace N, IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) (W.val.preimage g.hom.hom).ι ∧ IsIso (W.val.fromPreimage g.hom.hom) ∧ pointImage (W.val.preimage g.hom.hom).ι = {v : Point V.obj.obj | ∃ (T : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj T ⟶ Y.obj.obj), IsEtale a ∧ ∃ (U : Over S) (q : yoneda.obj U ⟶ V.obj.obj) (p : U ⟶ T), IsPullback q (yoneda.map p) f.hom.hom a ∧ ∃ x : U.left, schemePointMap q x = v ∧ p.left.IsQuasiFiniteAtPoint x}
lean.note: The fixed normalization is specified by its integral-factorization universal property. The quasi-finite point predicate is expanded using the recorded Stacks scheme predicate on an actual representing pullback over an etale target chart.
